A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HATCH study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v3 retains Appendices A-E and adds Appendix F; no material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HATCH benchmark evaluations, component and reasoning-modality ablations, training dynamics, and grid-resolution experiments in Tables 1-4 and Figures 3-5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results and experimental analyses in Tables 1-4 and Figures 3-5. Retained results still constitute original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The PaStA alignment objective, staged training procedure, ActoR action generation, and GRPO reward components remain unchanged. Sections 3.2-3.4 and Appendices A-D show no algorithmic or architectural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions train using SPAR-7M and evaluate on SPAR-Bench-MV, MindCube-Tiny, MMSI-Bench, SPAR-Bench-SI, and CV-Bench. Dynamic scenes and automatically estimated geometry are discussed as future directions, without additional evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain the same comparator sets. v3 corrects the prose label LLaVA-OneVision-7B to LLaVA-OneVision-4B, matching the 4B comparator already listed in v1 Tables 1 and 4; this does not establish a changed evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The 10,000-example training sample, 10% cold-start subset, backbone, reported GRPO settings, metrics, and benchmark subset usage remain unchanged. The newly specified action-discretization values are implementation disclosures, without a reported revision to the settings used.

E4.justification: The component ablations, grid-resolution sweep, training curves, reasoning-modality comparison, and qualitative example are retained. Appendix F explains existing weaknesses and argues for noise tolerance, but adds no measured robustness test, ablation, or empirical case study.

E5.justification: No changes to run counts, seed reporting, or statistical procedures are documented. Tables retain point estimates, and Figure 3 retains the same shaded training curves without additional explanation of the bands.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 corrects gains over Qwen2.5-VL-3B from +17.8 to +28.7 points on SPAR-Bench-MV and from +14.9 to +12.4 on MindCube-Tiny. These agree with unchanged Table 1 scores: 53.6 versus 24.9 and 50.2 versus 37.8. The underlying experimental scores and plotted findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly makes explicit the assumption that a single, static 3D structure underlies all viewpoints, grounding the correspondence supervision. Mathematical definitions, losses, reward equations, and Appendix C remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The main PaStA/ActoR contributions and benchmark-performance claims are retained. However, the Introduction and Conclusion now explicitly restrict the work to static multi-view geometry and place temporal inconsistencies outside its scope, qualifying the stated applicability.

C2.justification: New Appendix F substantially expands v1's limited discussion of weaknesses. It attributes poor Rotation performance to insufficient overlap and some MMSI failures to temporal inconsistency, explains restrictions imposed by geometric annotations, and argues for moderate-noise tolerance. The conclusion incorporates these limitations and corresponding future directions. These explanations are qualitative rather than newly validated findings.

D1.justification: Appendix F.2 newly specifies action preprocessing at 0.1 m translation and 10-degree rotation increments. The acknowledgements identify the TSUBAME4.0 computing facility. Appendix D's hyperparameters remain unchanged, and the existing project-page link is relocated without a documented access change.

R1.justification: v3 adds Depth Anything 3 as a potential source of estimated geometry and compares annotation dependence with already-cited spatial-reasoning approaches. Langley (2000) also appears as a new bibliography entry. Most other reference changes update the same works' authorship or publication metadata, including MindCube and Qwen2.5-VL.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are preserved. v3 adds a scope paragraph, limitations appendix, and acknowledgements; expands the conclusion; corrects wording and the LLaVA model label; and updates affiliation, conference, and bibliography text.

P2.justification: All five figures and five tables are retained with the same scientific displays. v3 changes front-page placement of affiliations and the project link, adds conference information, and reflows surrounding text. Table 1's caption additionally defines 'Rot.' as 'Rotation'.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects erroneous performance differences, reconciles the LLaVA model label, discloses action-discretization settings, and explains important applicability limits that v1 left underdeveloped. These changes improve reporting accuracy and transparency while preserving the experimental evidence. The new failure-mechanism and noise-tolerance arguments remain qualitative, so the overall gain is limited.
